jobs.jd_excerpt:
With roughly seven out of eight enterprise workloads still running on-premises or on mainframe, the opportunity to help the world's largest organizations move to the cloud is enormous. AWS Transform is building a platform that combines AI-driven automation with deep infrastructure and software engineering to analyze, plan, and execute large-scale application migrations. As a Software Development Engineer on this team, you will work across the full stack, from designing the distributed systems and services that power migration workflows to building the intelligent agents that reason about complex legacy environments. You will own the design and delivery of features and components, from understanding customer needs through implementation, testing, and production operations. You will work with senior engineers on system design, write high-quality, well-tested code, and help operate the services you build. Your work will directly shape how enterprises move their most critical workloads to AWS. You will collaborate closely with senior engineers, product managers, and customer-facing teams to make sure what you build turns into real customer outcomes. If you are excited about solving hard, high-impact problems with strong engineering fundamentals and applied AI skills, we would love to hear from you. Key job responsibilities Design, build, and operate distributed services and AI-powered agents that analyze legacy codebases, plan migration strategies, and execute transformations end to end. Drive the end-to-end design of the features you own, making trade-offs across scalability, performance, and security, and communicate across teams to influence architectural decisions on shared interfaces and infrastructure. Write well-documented, production-quality code that sets an example for others, and make sure solutions are testable and easy for others to extend. Play a key technical role on the team in aligning engineering work with customer needs, turning requirements into product features and delivering them incrementally. Mentor teammates through design and code reviews, foster engineering best practices, and take part in interviewing and recruiting. A day in the life Your morning might start with a design review where you present your approach for a new service component that automates a migration step previously done by hand. After working through the details with a senior engineer, you shift to writing and reviewing code, working on infrastructure plumbing one hour and refining an agent's decision logic the next. In the afternoon you meet with your product manager and a customer-facing teammate to go over feedback from an enterprise customer pilot and turn it into improvements for your feature. You wrap up by updating operational dashboards and tuning alerts for a service you helped launch. About the team AWS Transform sits within the Agentic AI organization at Amazon Web Services and is focused on building the next generation of autonomous migration services. The team partners closely with go-to-market, professional services, and enterprise customers to turn complex modernization challenges into repeatable, well-engineered solutions that blend systems infrastructure with applied AI. We are at an early and exciting stage of product development, which means your contributions will directly shape the platform's architecture and roadmap. We value curiosity, collaboration, and a willingness to experiment, and we are committed to building an inclusive environment where every team member can do their best work.

    appropriate to the solution and mission requirements.

    deployment practices.

    contribute to the development of analytical methodologies and best practices.

About Reducto Nearly 80% of enterprise data is in unstructured formats like PDFs PDFs are the status quo for enterprise knowledge in nearly every industry. Insurance claims, financial statements, invoices, and health records are all stored in a structure that’s simply impractical for use in digital workflows. This isn’t an inconvenience—it’s a critical bottleneck that leads to dozens of wasted hours every week. Traditional approaches fail at reliably extracting information in complex PDFs OCR and even more sophisticated ML approaches work for simple text documents but are unreliable for anything more complex. Text from different columns are jumbled together, figures are ignored, and tables are a nightmare to get right. Overcoming this usually requires a large engineering effort dedicated to building specialized pipelines for every document type you work with. Our pipelines are modern and up to date, and we use AI throughout our work to move faster. You'll collaborate with business stakeholders, data engineering teams, and fellow analysts to modernize reporting capabilities, enhance self-service analytics, and continuously improve data quality and operational efficiency. Build and enhance Looker Explores, semantic data models, dashboards, and self-service reporting solutions to support merchandising analytics and business decision-making. Responsibilities: Collect, clean, organize, and analyze datasets to identify trends and opportunities. Write SQL queries to extract and analyze data from databases. Develop and maintain dashboards, reports, and visualizations using tools like Power BI, Tableau, or Looker. Monitor business performance metrics and KPIs to identify areas for improvement. Use Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets for data manipulation and reporting. Conduct exploratory data analysis to support business decisions. Validate datasets and maintain data accuracy. Collaborate with teams to understand business and analytical needs. Present findings and recommendations to technical and non-technical stakeholders. Assist in automating reports and improving data workflows. Requirements: Master's degree in Business Analytics, Data Analytics, Data Science, Computer Science, Information Systems, Statistics, or a related field. 0–1 year of experience in data analytics, business analytics, business intelligence, or a related role. Basic knowledge of Python or R for data analysis and automation. Understanding of business metrics, KPIs, and performance reporting. Skills in data cleaning, validation, and database fundamentals. jobs.jd_excerpt:
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is building the foundational services developers use to create, deploy, and operate production-ready AI agents at scale. AgentCore Harness, launched at AWS Summit New York in June 2026, provides a managed agent loop that enables customers to define an agent through configuration rather than build and operate orchestration infrastructure themselves. Customers specify their model, instructions, tools, skills, memory, and execution limits. AgentCore Harness manages the agent loop, secure execution environment, session isolation, identity, networking, observability, and deployment lifecycle. This allows developers to move quickly from an idea to a production agent while retaining the flexibility to integrate custom tools, models, and environments. As a Software Development Engineer, you will design, implement, test, deploy, and operate core components across the Harness control plane and data plane. You will solve challenging distributed systems problems involving agent execution, session state, tool orchestration, security, scalability, reliability, and low-latency streaming. You will own features throughout their lifecycle, contribute to technical designs, and deliver high-quality solutions for customers. Harness sits at the intersection of AgentCore Runtime, Memory, Gateway, Identity, Observability, Browser, Code Interpreter, and Evaluations. You will collaborate with engineers across these services to integrate capabilities, improve cross-service APIs, and reduce friction throughout the agent development lifecycle. A central part of this role is making sophisticated agent capabilities dramatically easier to use. You will work backward from customer needs to turn complex infrastructure and orchestration tasks into intuitive configuration, sensible defaults, reusable templates, and guided workflows. Your work will help customers move from an idea to a secure, observable, production-ready agent in minutes while preserving the flexibility advanced builders need for customization. You will help develop capabilities that make agent development faster and more accessible. This may include simplifying how customers connect tools and memory, building richer agent templates and skills, automating permissions and resource wiring, shortening the build-test-deploy loop, and creating safer ways to evaluate and release changes. This is an opportunity to join a newly launched service at an early stage, contribute to its architecture and customer experience, and deliver capabilities with broad industry impact. Machine learning experience is helpful but not required. We are looking for strong engineers with distributed systems experience, sound technical judgment, a commitment to operational excellence, and the ability to deliver in a fast-moving environment. Key job responsibilities - Design, build, test, deploy, and operate highly available control plane APIs, data plane services, and managed agent loops for production AI agents. - Build secure, isolated execution capabilities spanning tool orchestration, memory, context management, streaming, identity, networking, observability, and failure handling. - Develop integrations between Amazon Bedrock and third-party models, AgentCore services, MCP servers, AWS Step Functions, Strands Agents, and customer-defined environments. - Implement versioning, endpoints, progressive deployment, rollback, evaluation, and optimization capabilities that help customers safely improve agent behavior. - Analyze and improve latency, scalability, availability, resource efficiency, and cost controls across multi-tenant workloads. - Simplify the developer journey across APIs, SDKs, CLI, console, infrastructure as code, and local workflows by building cohesive abstractions, templates, defaults, and automation. - Work directly with customers and partner teams to identify and reduce friction, accelerate time to production, and balance approachable experiences with the flexibility advanced builders need. - Contribute to architectural decisions within Harness and collaborate with teams across AgentCore. Help raise the engineering bar through design reviews, operational readiness, code reviews, knowledge sharing, and mentoring.

jobs.jd_excerpt: Job Description About the Team The Autonomous Vehicle Microcontrollers team develops embedded platform software that provides the foundation for AV systems. Our software communicates with sensors, supports vehicle operation, provides observability, manages system health, and enables reliable operation of vehicle and platform functions. About the Role As a Software Engineer on the AV MCU Platform team, you will independently own moderate-scope software features, components, or sub-projects related to MCU01. You will contribute across the development lifecycle‚ from requirements and design through implementation, integration, testing, debugging, documentation, and release support. You will work closely with systems, hardware, safety, cybersecurity, integration, and validation teams to deliver production-quality embedded software. Come build the future of self-driving at GM. What You’ll Do (Responsibilities) Reproduce and diagnose software failures using logs, traces, debugger data, telemetry, test evidence, and controlled experiments. Perform structured root-cause analysis for crashes, memory faults, timing issues, race conditions, communication failures, watchdog resets, and unexpected state transitions as applicable. Design, develop, integrate, and maintain embedded C software for multi-core microcontrollers. Implement moderate-scope features, enhancements, integrations, and defect fixes within the assigned software component or subsystem. Develop across the applicable automotive embedded software stack, including BSP, BSW, middleware, RTOS services, drivers, and application software. Write maintainable, modular, efficient, and testable code consistent with team coding standards. Implement robust handling for initialization, state transitions, communication errors, diagnostics, degraded operation, watchdog events, and fault recovery as applicable. Analyze the impact of software changes on interfaces, timing, memory, CPU utilization, configuration, and dependent components. Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications) Bachelors degree in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering, or a related STEM field; equivalent relevant experience may be considered. Ability to diagnose software issues using logs, traces, debuggers, test results, and other technical evidence. 2+ years of experience building and shipping production quality embedded software Background in C Embedded Software development Understanding software development lifecycle practices, source control, code reviews, continuous integration, and issue tracking. jobs.jd_excerpt: <div class="content-intro"><h3><strong>Who We Are</strong></h3> <p>Verkada is transforming how organizations protect their people and places with an integrated, privacy-sensitive AI-powered platform that includes solutions for video security, access control, air quality sensors, alarms, intercoms, and visitor management.&nbsp;</p> <p>We’ve got serious momentum in the market: more than 30,000 customers (including 100+ of the Fortune 500), <a href="https://www.cnbc.com/2025/12/03/verkada-capitalg-valuation-security.html">a $5.8B valuation</a>, more than $1 billion in annualized bookings, and backing from CapitalG, Sequoia Capital, General Catalyst, Felicis Ventures, Next47 and more. Physical AI is one of the most consequential technology shifts of our time, and Verkada is at the center of it.</p> <p>You can look at all kinds of communities to see our platform’s impact in the world. It's the retailer that uses our agentic AI to deter theft before it happens. The warehouse that uses AI-powered alerts to make sure its team is protected on the floor with proper PPE. The school that’s alerted to a threat in real-time and triggers a lockdown in seconds, not minutes. We’re rapidly scaling this impact: today, more than 2 million Verkada devices are deployed across 170+ countries.&nbsp;</p></div><h3><strong>About the Role</strong></h3> <div>We are looking for software engineers who thrive in a high growth environment working alongside teammates to launch products and features that will be utilized by customers across the globe. About Tutor We believe robots are the biggest lever we have to making the physical world a better, more affordable place. But robots are a rounding error in our society: nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t even have a single robot, and robots have yet to make their way into our homes or places of business. Tutor Intelligence is changing that. Tutor is a robotics research and deployment company, building generally capable robot hardware and artificial intelligence to enable robots to go where no robots have gone before. Sonny is a semi-humanoid robot with frontier dexterity approaching the human form. Cassie does back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for businesses from family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Tutor robots are manufactured at scale and operate as a network, combining the whole fleet’s learned experience to train ever more capable robot artificial intelligence. Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, our team is full stack: we design and manufacture robot hardware, train our own models, work directly with the smallest and largest end-customers, and maintain our fleet across the United States. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems. Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world. The Role As our first Applied AI Engineer on Go-to-Market, you'll build the operating system for how Tutor finds, wins, and grows customers across the physical economy. You'll design the process flows and change the shape of the work, and you'll do it by writing a lot of software: building whole workflows, tools, and AI agents from scratch rather than configuring someone else's. This is a technical role where you write and own software, and you'll embed as a true member of our go-to-market team, owning outcomes for that team through technology. You'll sit in the GTM room alongside our account executives, sales enablement, and demand generation, and you'll treat go-to-market as part of the wider Tutor system: our robots, deployments, data, and the AI that runs them. Most of your work will be self-directed: start from a goal, and build the system that fits around it. You'll join our forward-deployed AI engineering team: a strategic team of engineers already embedded across deployment, manufacturing, maintenance, and hardware and software engineering, using AI to change how each of those functions works. You'll be its first engineer dedicated to go-to-market. You'll start by taking over and extending go-to-market tools we've already built. From there you'll steward the area as the business grows, using the tools alongside the team and improving them to handle more scale and complexity.

jobs.jd_excerpt: <div class="content-intro"><p>Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.</p></div><h3>ABOUT THE TEAM</h3> <p>At Anduril, our Software Engineers specialize in solving complex, real-world problems through cutting-edge algorithms and intelligent software integrations. Operating in small, innovative teams, we push the boundaries of what's possible to deliver advanced technologies with mission-critical applications. Our commitment doesn't end with academic research or proof-of-concept experiments; we measure our success by the real-world impact of our deployed solutions. Inspired by Arthur C. Clarke’s vision — “Any sufficiently advanced technology is indistinguishable from magic” — we aim to achieve groundbreaking results in target tracking, state estimation, and situational awareness. We are currently seeking highly talented technologists to join our mission and redefine the future of defense technology.</p> <h4><strong>WHAT YOU WILL DO:</strong></h4> <ul> <li>Define and influence the direction of a small team, leveraging your subject-matter expertise in target tracking and state estimation.</li> <li>Prototype and deploy state-of-the-art algorithms for tracking, multi-sensor data fusion, and state estimation in agile, iterative development environments.</li> <li>Develop high-performance software for real-time systems, ranging from tactical implementations to simulation environments and decision support tools.</li> <li>Design and implement robust filters, estimators, and probabilistic reasoning systems that enable actionable insights from noisy, ambiguous, or incomplete sensor data.</li> <li>Analyze system performance using high-fidelity simulations, innovative modeling tools, and rigorous statistical techniques to validate the benefits of our technology.</li> <li>Drive customer success by customizing algorithms and software for mission-critical use cases, including real-time tracking and sensor fusion.</li> <li>Integrate tracking and estimation technologies into the broader software development lifecycle, from requirements definition through testing and optimization.</li> <li>Translate technical progress into clear, actionable insights for diverse stakeholders, including colleagues and end-users.</li> </ul> <h4><strong>REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS</strong></h4> <ul data-list-tree="true" data-indent="0" data-border="0"> <li>Proficiency in algorithm design, software development, and statistical modeling with programming expertise in C/C++, Python, and Matlab.</li> <li>Strong knowledge of target tracking techniques, such as Kalman filters, particle filters, and multi-target tracking algorithms (e.g., JPDA, MHT, or PHD filters).</li> <li>Experience in state estimation, including Bayesian filtering, sensor fusion, and recursive estimation techniques.</li> <li>Solid understanding of applied mathematics, including linear algebra, optimization, probability, and stochastic processes.</li> <li>Knowledge of signal processing techniques for interpreting diverse sensor data (e.g., radar, lidar, EO/IR).</li> <li>Familiarity with big data pipelines, NoSQL databases, and the efficient handling of large-scale sensor data.</li> <li>Background in machine learning as applied to target tracking and recognition, including clustering, classification, and anomaly detection techniques.</li> <li>Ability to engineer robust systems for estimation theory, adaptive filtering, controls, and complex signal environments.</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to work across development lifecycles, from prototyping to optimizing production systems.</li> <li>Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Top Secret security clearance.</li> </ul> <p><em data-stringify-type="italic">We request transcripts as part of the early application process to understand your academic background and how your coursework supports the skills deemed critical for the role. Transcripts help us assess your technical and analytical abilities, complementing our interview process in which we also evaluate practical experience and cultural fit. If you choose not to share your transcripts, you will need to provide detailed information regarding your academic performance in relevant courses, including projects and coursework specifics, to ensure we evaluate your academic accomplishments properly. If you do provide academic transcripts, feel free to redact non-technical information (e.g., student ID, dates, non-technical coursework, etc.). Unofficial transcripts obtained online acceptable for this assessment.</em></p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="title">US Salary Range</div><div class="pay-range"><span>$167,000</span><span class="divider">&mdash;</span><span>$222,000 USD</span></div></div></div><div class=&qu

Our team, Global E-Commerce Content Recommendation, owns the end-to-end recommendation stack for e-commerce video and image-text content on TikTok worldwide — retrieval, ranking, and multi-queue blending; supply ecosystem and cold start; and the browsing-to-purchase experience for hundreds of millions of users. We are building what we intend to be the most advanced recommendation system in the world, on top of a two-sided marketplace that is still growing fast. Many of the problems that matter most here — what to optimize, how to know it worked, how to treat a brand-new seller fairly — have no settled answer anywhere in the industry. We are looking for talented individuals to join our team. As a graduate, you will get opportunities to pursue bold ideas, tackle complex challenges, and unlock limitless growth. Successful candidates must be able to commit to an onboarding date by the end of the year. Please state your availability and graduation date clearly in your resume. Candidates can apply to a maximum of two positions and will be considered for jobs in the order you apply. The application limit is applicable to our Company and its affiliates' jobs globally. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis - we encourage you to apply early. Responsibilities: Optimize the recommendation models across the full funnel: You own the models behind TikTok Shop's product, short-video, and livestream recommendation — retrieval, pre-ranking, ranking, re-ranking, and multi-queue blending — and every iteration ships to real traffic. Core threads: Ranking and retrieval models. Iterate the model architectures that carry the funnel: multi-task and multi-objective learning from click through conversion and GMV; multi-scenario, multi-format joint modelling; and the sample, label, and debiasing design that decides what the model actually learns. User interest modelling. Ultra-long behavior sequences (10K+ events) with real trade-offs between positional-encoding extrapolation, attention cost, and online latency and storage; decoupling stable preferences from seasonal demand, momentary impulses, and needs already satisfied; and mining implicit negative feedback — impressions without clicks, consecutive skips, fast swipes — at every stage of the funnel. Multimodal representation learning. Combine product images, text, and video content with behavioural data into high-quality item and user representations. Re-ranking, blending, and exploration. List-level decisions rather than pointwise scores: multi-queue blending across content types, diversity and repetition control, and exploration mechanisms that surface interests users have not yet expressed — while breaking the recommendation feedback loop. Design the cold-start and content-ecosystem mechanisms: New products, new livestream hosts, and new creators arrive in volume every day. Do original work on open problems. Long-term value modelling, repurchase and retention, transaction attribution, fatigue modelling, new-user recommendation, incremental value modelling, LLM4Rec — the frontier problems of a real recommendation system, where the industry has no standard answers. Qualifications Minimum Qualifications: Individuals who are completing or have recently completed a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mathematics, Statistics or a related discipline. Solid algorithms and data-structures fundamentals and excellent coding ability: clean, efficient, reproducible code. Solid foundations in machine learning, probability, and statistics: you understand the assumptions behind a model and where it breaks, and you can explain why a method works and under what conditions it fails — not just how to call the API. Fluent in a deep-learning framework (PyTorch / TensorFlow) and at least one large-scale data-processing tool (Spark / Flink / SQL); proficient in Python, with working C++ and Linux skills. Data sense and experimental rigor: you can locate the real cause behind a metric movement, and you understand A/B test design, statistical confidence, and the common pitfalls. Fast learner, clear communicator, good collaborator. Preferred Qualifications: Research or engineering experience in recommendation, search, ads, information retrieval, NLP, or large-scale ML systems. Awards in Kaggle, Tianchi, or RecSys Challenge, or an ACM-ICPC / NOI competition background. Hands-on experience with causal inference, online learning / bandits, graph neural networks, sequence modelling, or large-scale distributed training. Heavy user of AI coding and agentic workflows for building systems and optimizing models. jobs.jd_excerpt: Why Rogo Our mission is to transform global finance by empowering professionals at the world's top investment banks, private equity funds, and investment firms with AI that delivers unparalleled speed, accuracy, and insight. We're not just improving financial workflows; we're redefining them. This is a unique opportunity to join a generational company driving transformation in one of the most important industries in the world. With a rapidly growing, global client base, proven product-market fit, and backing from world-class investors, we are scaling quickly and defining a new category of enterprise AI. Our team is sharp, motivated, and deeply committed to Rogo’s mission. We take ownership of complex problems and stay relentlessly focused on our users. If you thrive in a fast-paced environment, demand excellence, and want to help build the future of finance, we invite you to join us. The Role Analytics at Rogo defines the metrics, runs the pipelines behind them, and turns both into decisions and a better product. We’re hiring a Data Engineer to take full ownership of our Analytics infrastructure and build it into something that scales confidently with the company. This is a hands-on, high-leverage role: pipelines, orchestration, and reliability. If you are an experienced data engineer excited about how your role can evolve at an AI-native organization, this is the opportunity for you. In many ways this is also a product role. Rogo productizes how we use our own data — many of our Analytical features began as internal analytics work. You will be expected to know the product as well as any engineer here, because the systems you build both measure it and support its development. We expect everyone at Rogo to take ownership of making our product better for our users. What You Will Own Own analytics infrastructure: the ETL pipelines, Snowflake, dbt models, orchestration, and the reliability of all of it. Analytics evals: design and run the evaluation and testing layer for our agentic analytics surfaces — internal agents that answer thousands of questions a quarter, and the customer-facing analytics our enterprise admins rely on. This is one of the defining problems of doing analytics at an AI company. Own core KPIs: the definitions, the pipelines that produce them, and the documentation that makes them legible. When a number moves, you can say whether the pipeline broke, the definition changed, or the business moved. Know the product inside and out: develop the same depth of product understanding as any engineer or salesperson at Rogo. Turn internal work into product: partner with engineering and product where our analytics infrastructure becomes a customer-facing feature. Pick up a lane of analytics work: as the foundation solidifies, take a domain of your own and go deep, so the team’s judgment grows alongside its infrastructure. What You Will Need 5+ years of professional experience in data engineering, analytics engineering, or a closely related role, with a track record of owning production data systems. Deep SQL proficiency and fluency in a modern cloud data warehouse (Snowflake preferred) Hands-on dbt experience: models, tests, macros, incremental strategies, and a real point of view on what makes a well-structured transformation layer. Strong Python for pipeline and transformation work, and comfort with orchestration and modern ETL tooling. You have a real point of view on keeping a fast refresh cadence as event volume geometrically increases with our business: partitioning strategies, incremental model design, storage tiering, etc. Genuine fluency with AI products. You’ve used agentic tools seriously and have a working picture of what happens between a question and an answer: retrieval, tool calls, model turns, and where cost accrues. Real curiosity about the business. You care about and take ownership of what a number means, not only that the job ran. Comfort operating with autonomy across multiple stakeholders and domains. Bonus Growth-stage experience, or familiarity with the scale of data Rogo will be handling twelve months from now. Experience building evals or test harnesses for LLM-powered systems. Experience with single- and multi-tenant customer architectures. Familiarity with Salesforce, Intercom, or usage-based billing data models (Metronome or similar). Experience with third-party financial or B2B data vendors (LSEG, FactSet, Crunchbase, ZoomInfo, Apollo, or similar). Background in financial services, enterprise SaaS, or vertical AI. Who You Are You thrive in fast-paced environments. You are high-intensity and care a lot about what you do, and you're ecstatic to work at a startup. You are ambitious. You have fun solving problems that others think are impossible. You are curious. You find joy in learning about AI, technology, and finance. You are an owner. You are autonomous, self-directed, and comfortable working with ambiguity. You are collaborative, organized, thoughtful, and kind. Why Join Rogo? Up and to the right: Rogo has strong product adoption with the world's leading financial institutions, and we are still early. The upside is enormous. Extraordinary team: we take talent density seriously. You'll do the best work of your career alongside some of the sharpest people in AI and finance. A one-of-one problem: bringing AI to the core of how Wall Street works is one of the most ambitious, technically demanding, and consequential problems today. There is nowhere else you can work on it at this scale. Real ownership: You'll own real surface area and watch the world's most sophisticated users rely on your work. Always at the frontier: we work at the edge of what the best models can do and turn it into products people trust. If you're obsessed with AI, this is where it's happening.

jobs.jd_excerpt: <div class="content-intro"><p>GiveCampus is the world's leading fundraising platform for non-profit educational institutions. Trusted by millions of donors and 1,300+ colleges, universities, and K-12 schools, our mission is to help advance the quality, the affordability, and the accessibility of education. At our current pace, we will facilitate $100 billion in charitable giving over the next decade–enough money to send more than 1 million students to college, tuition-free.</p> <p>GiveCampus is backed by leading investors including Y Combinator, but we’re also practitioners of <a href="https://go.givecampus.com/blog/reflecting-on-7-years-of-sustainable-growth/">Sustainable Growth</a>: we’ve made the <a href="https://www.inc.com/profile/givecampus">Inc. 5000 list</a> of America's fastest-growing private companies each of the last five years and we’ve been profitable nine of the last 10. In 2025, we <a href="https://go.givecampus.com/blog/our-second-tender-offer-in-three-years-and-what-it-means-for-the-future-of-givecampus/">celebrated a $140 million growth investment</a> that included a major liquidity event for GiveCampus employees–the second in less than three years.&nbsp;</p> <p>Our purpose-driven team of 130+ is located in 30+ states across the US: team members work from anywhere they choose. We have a beautiful 12,000sf office in Washington, DC that is available for people to use whenever they want, and we regularly organize team meet-ups, visit partner institutions, and host retreats in various locations.&nbsp;</p> <p>While we operate at meaningful scale, we’re still small relative to the commercial and social good opportunities in front of us. Every GiveCampus employee plays a meaningful role in shaping what comes next, and we're growing the team in support of our ambitious plans–including a $100 million investment in AI product development. If you believe in the transformative power of education and want to join a fast-growing, mission-driven company, you’ll fit right in.</p> <p><br><strong data-stringify-type="bold">Location:</strong>&nbsp;This is a remote-first role based in the U.S. While we embrace flexible, distributed work, we also value in-person connection. Team members are expected to attend multiple company-wide and team-specific onsites throughout the year.</p></div><h2>About the role</h2> <p>Every donation that moves through the GiveCampus platform passes through the Online Giving team's code. We run Agile, mostly Scrum with one-week sprints, and we ship to production multiple times a day.</p> <h2>Our stack</h2> <ul> <li>Ruby on Rails</li> <li>React</li> <li>Postgres and Redis</li> <li>Stripe, Spreedly, and PayPal for payment processing</li> <li>AWS with ArgoCD and Kubernetes for hosting and application management</li> </ul> <h2>What you'll do</h2> <ul> <li>Build and maintain donor-facing giving forms, giving pages, and admin tools with a focus on conversion, accessibility, and mobile-first design.</li> <li>Build and harden payment flows—one-time, recurring, and memberships—across Stripe, ACH, and Digital Wallets, with reliability and observability in mind.</li> <li>Work across the full stack, from UI components to backend services to database queries and performance.</li> <li>Own features and small-to-medium projects end to end: technical design and work breakdown, coding, automated testing, deployment, and support in production.</li> <li>Partner closely with your pod's Tech Lead, Product Manager, Designer, and fellow engineers to turn user needs and business goals into technical solutions, and speak up early when you spot blockers or trade-offs.</li> <li>Participate actively in sprint planning, story scoping, and estimation, including thorough review of acceptance criteria.</li> <li>Write clean, well-tested, well-documented code, and give and receive thoughtful code review.</li> <li>Contribute to team initiatives like technical debt refinement and coding standards, and help teammates get unstuck.</li> <li>Participate in interviewing and onboarding as the team grows.</li> <li>Support the platform on a rotational basis, including team-based support and a paired 24/7 on-call rotation. You'll build the processes, set the standards, and make sure the right material, with the right paperwork, reaches the right work order on the planned date.</p> <p>This is a high-impact, high-visibility role for someone who is both analytical and hands-on. By taking advantage of all structured and unstructured data — securing and protecting private information more effectively — Elastic’s complete, cloud-based solutions for search, security, and observability help organizations deliver on the promise of AI.</p></div><h3><strong>What is The Role</strong></h3> <p>This is a hands-on build role that will develop and maintain HR's data pipelines on our GCP/BigQuery/dbt data model, with an AI-powered analytics layer on top. Core platform infrastructure is provisioned centrally; you'll help configure HR-specific pipelines and dbt modeling work on top of it, in partnership with our data scientist, and stand up recruiting reporting and insights as the first production use case on the new stack. This role reports directly to the Director of HR Analytics, with high visibility into architecture and stakeholder-facing decisions from day one.</p> <p>Your mission is to move the organization away (e.g., Workday, Greenhouse) via its reporting or API layer. jobs.jd_excerpt: <p>CHAOS Industries is redefining modern defense with a multi-product portfolio that gives the ultimate advantage—domain dominance. The company's products are powered by Coherent Distributed Networks (CDN™), empowering warfighters, commercial air operators, and border protection teams to act faster, adapt rapidly, and stay ahead of evolving threats.&nbsp;</p> <p>CHAOS Industries was founded in 2022 and has raised a total of $1 billion in funding from leading investors, including 8VC, Accel, and Valor Equity Partners. The company is headquartered in Los Angeles, with offices in Washington, D.C., San Francisco, San Diego, and London. For more information, please visit&nbsp;<a href="https://www.chaosinc.com">www.chaosinc.com</a>.</p> <p><strong>The Role:</strong></p> <p>We're hiring one of the first software engineers on our electro-optical team. Today that means long-range EO/IR sensors. In future it could mean sensors on mobile and airborne platforms. Wherever the sensor sits, the job is the software that makes it, and every sensor around it, act as one system.</p> <p>This is a software engineering role first. You don't need to be a camera or computer vision specialist. You do need to be an excellent engineer who is curious about physical systems and understands how real sensors behave: they drift, they disagree with each other, and a field test doesn't care what the simulation said.</p> <p>You'll join a small, elite team that takes its own work into the field. You'll test live, change code live, and see how it holds up on the next flight. The capabilities you build will push the frontier of what these systems can do, and few engineers anywhere get to work this close to the hardware, the mission and the result.</p> <p>We're also changing how we build software. The aim is to take a feature or a new capability and develop as much of it as possible without real hardware, then push it up the chain: through simulation, through hardware in the loop, and on to full end-to-end tests in the real world. Simulation will keep improving, but real hardware will always have the final say. So we're building the harnesses and graphs that carry a capability through every one of those stages, with AI doing as much of the work as it can be trusted with. The end state is fully autonomous, end-to-end tests run against real hardware at our test sites. This is what you'll be building.</p> <p><strong>What You'll Build:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Software that works on any sensor. Code that stays generic across many different camera heads and configurations while still hitting its performance bar, and flexes to whatever the mission and the customer demand.</li> <li>The path from desk to field. Harnesses and graphs that take a capability from first commit through simulation and hardware in the loop to a full end-to-end test, with as little manual effort as possible.</li> <li>Autonomous field testing. The system that runs complete tests against real hardware at our test sites on its own, and reports back what happened.</li> <li>Better simulation and replay. So more of every feature can be built and proven before it touches hardware.</li> <li>Multi-sensor integration. The interfaces, timing and data flow that let radar, cameras and other sensors work as one system.</li> <li>Fielded software. Deployment, monitoring and live fixes for systems running on edge hardware at test and customer sites.</li> </ul> <p><br><strong>This Role Is Not:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Algorithm research. You'll build and ship software, not invent new detection or tracking algorithms.</li> <li>Physics modeling. You won't be building high-fidelity physics models in MATLAB or Simulink.</li> <li>Applied machine learning. You won't be training models on sensor data.</li> <li>Pure DevOps. You'll run infrastructure, but most of your time goes into writing software other engineers depend on.</li> </ul> <p><br><strong>What We're Looking For:</strong></p> <p>We care more about strong engineering fundamentals and curiosity than about any specific technology or domain.</p> <ul> <li>3+ years of professional software engineering, including owning a production system end to end: you designed it, shipped it, and fixed it when it broke.</li> <li>A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Physics or a related field, or equivalent experience.</li> <li>Strong Python. You build services and tools other engineers depend on, not just scripts and notebooks.</li> <li>Comfort with Linux, Docker, networking and CI. You can get a multi-service system running on hardware you've never touched before.</li> <li>Real leverage from AI coding tools such as Cursor or Claude Code, with a considered view on what to delegate to them and what not to. We treat them as a multiplier on skills you already have: you should be able to write, explain and debug your own code without them.</li> <li>Grounding in the physical world, whether from an engineering degree, hands-on work with hardware, sensors or robotics, or field time with systems that had to work outside the lab. Strong data storytelling, executive communication, and stakeholder influence skills, with the ability to drive alignment without formal authority. Experience in medical devices, healthcare, regulated industries, and/or high-tech environments preferred. jobs.jd_excerpt: Equifax is where you can power your possible. If you want to achieve your true potential, chart new paths, develop new skills, collaborate with bright minds, and make a meaningful impact, we want to hear from you. Equifax is seeking creative, high-energy and driven software engineers with hands-on development skills to work on a variety of meaningful projects. Our software engineering positions provide you the opportunity to join a team of talented engineers working with leading-edge technology. You are ideal for this position if you are a forward-thinking, committed, and enthusiastic software engineer who is passionate about technology. What you’ll do Perform general application development activities, including unit testing, code deployment to development environment and technical documentation. Works on one or more projects, making contributions to unfamiliar code written by team members. Participates in estimation process, use case specifications, reviews of test plans and test cases, requirements, and project planning. Diagnose and resolve performance issues. Documents code/processes so that any other developer is able to dive in with minimal effort. Develop, and operate high scale applications from the backend to UI layer, focusing on operational excellence, security and scalability. Apply modern software development practices (serverless computing, microservices architecture, CI/CD, infrastructure-as-code, etc.). Work across teams to integrate our systems with existing internal systems, Data Fabric, CSA Toolset. Participate in technology roadmap and architecture discussions to turn business requirements and vision into reality. Participate in a tight-knit engineering team employing agile software development practices. Triage product or system issues and debug/track/resolve by analyzing the sources of issues and the impact on network, or service operations and quality. Able to write, debug, and troubleshoot code in mainstream open source technologies. Lead effort for Sprint deliverables, and solve problems with medium complexity What experience you need Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience 2+ years experience working with software design and Java, Python and Javascript programming languages 2+ years experience with software build management tools like Maven or Gradle 2+ years experience with HTML, CSS and frontend/web development 2+ years experience with software testing, performance, and quality engineering techniques and strategies 2+ years experience with Cloud technology: GCP, AWS, or Azure What could set you apart Self-starter that identifies/responds to priority shifts with minimal supervision UI development (e.g. HTML, JavaScript, Angular and Bootstrap) Experience with backend technologies such as JAVA/J2EE, SpringBoot, SOA and Microservices Source code control management systems (e.g. SVN/Git, Github) and build tools like Maven & Gradle. Agile environments (e.g. Scrum, XP) Relational databases (e.g. SQL Server, MySQL) Atlassian tooling (e.g. JIRA, Confluence, and Github) Developing with modern JDK (v1.7+) Automated Testing: JUnit, Selenium, LoadRunner, SoapUI We offer comprehensive compensation and healthcare packages, 401k matching, paid time off, and organizational growth potential through our online learning platform with guided career tracks. Are you ready to power your possible? Apply today, and get started on a path toward an exciting new career at Equifax, where you can make a difference! We work to help create seamless and positive experiences during life’s pivotal moments: applying for jobs or a mortgage, financing an education or buying a car. jobs.jd_excerpt: About The Role As a member of the Data team within the Go-to-Market organization, you will help build a data-driven culture, improve decision-making, and advance strategic initiatives through analytics. This is a full-stack data role spanning data modeling, metric definition, visualization, analysis, and self-service tooling. You will build trusted, scalable data sources and products that give the business reliable, actionable insights. The work calls for judgment: you will choose the tool, approach, and level of investment that best fit each problem, from a focused analysis to a durable production data product. As a core partner to the GTM organization, you will address both foundational and ad hoc analytics needs. You will turn complex data into clear narratives that help technical and non-technical audiences understand what is happening, why it matters, and what they should do next. In This Role, You Will Partner closely with GTM teams to proactively identify high-impact questions and translate business needs into data models, metrics, analyses, and scalable technical solutions. Define, source, validate, and operationalize the metrics that guide the business, helping teams incorporate them into planning and day-to-day decisions. Lead cross-functional data projects across established and emerging business areas, including setting the data strategy for greenfield domains. Build scalable data models and pipelines that integrate and transform data from multiple sources into trusted, accessible datasets. Create dashboards, reports, analytical tools, and other data products that enable stakeholders to answer questions independently. Own the lifecycle of metrics, analytical models, and data products from initial exploration and prototyping through production and ongoing maintenance. Choose the most effective approach for each problem—whether an analysis, metric, data model, visualization, or self-service product—based on the audience, urgency, complexity, and expected value. Exercise strong judgment when prioritizing competing requests, balancing immediate business needs with investments that improve the long-term quality and scalability of the data ecosystem. Use AI-assisted development tools to increase productivity while maintaining clear, tested, and maintainable code, data models, and documentation. Turn complex findings into clear, persuasive narratives through presentations, written memos, dashboards, and other formats suited to the audience. You Might Thrive in This Role If You Have 10+ years of experience in a relevant data role within fast-moving, results-oriented organizations. Can independently structure and own ambiguous, high-impact business problems from initial framing through recommendation and execution. Are highly autonomous, resourceful, and creative when navigating technical, operational, and stakeholder constraints. Exercise strong judgment when deciding what to prioritize, how deeply to invest, and when a quick answer should become a durable data product. Have deep SQL expertise and extensive experience working with large datasets and designing ETL workflows. Understand effective software and analytics engineering practices and can use AI tools to move faster without creating brittle systems, unclear code, or unnecessary complexity. Are proficient in a quantitative programming language, preferably Python. Have experience with BI tools such as Tableau or Looker and know how to enable effective self-service analytics. Have worked with custom visualization frameworks such as React, Streamlit, or Plotly Dash. Can turn complex analysis into persuasive stories using memos, presentations, dashboards, and other formats. Bring exceptional attention to detail and a strong commitment to accuracy. Have delivered significant business impact, ideally within Sales, Finance, Support, or another GTM function. Prime Video is a first-stop entertainment destination offering customers a vast collection of premium programming in one app available across thousands of devices. Prime members can customize their viewing experience and find their favorite movies, series, documentaries, and live sports – including Amazon MGM Studios-produced series and movies; licensed fan favorites; and programming from Prime Video subscriptions such as Apple TV+, HBO Max, Peacock, Crunchyroll and MGM+. All customers, regardless of whether they have a Prime membership or not, can rent or buy titles via the Prime Video Store, and can enjoy even more content for free with ads. Are you interested in shaping the future of entertainment? Prime Video's technology teams are creating best-in-class digital video experience. As a Prime Video team member, you’ll have end-to-end ownership of the product, user experience, design, and technology required to deliver state-of-the-art experiences for our customers. You’ll get to work on projects that are fast-paced, challenging, and varied. You’ll also be able to experiment with new possibilities, take risks, and collaborate with remarkable people. We’ll look for you to bring your diverse perspectives, ideas, and skill-sets to make Prime Video even better for our customers. With global opportunities for talented technologists, you can decide where a career Prime Video Tech takes you! Key job responsibilities The science challenges include: - Heterogeneous customer responses. The same customer responds differently to ads depending on what they’re watching, how engaged they are, and their broader streaming context. We need to understand and predict this variation to make better advertising decisions in real time. - Signal sparsity in streaming. Unlike search or retail advertising, streaming offers no clicks, no conversions, and limited direct feedback. We must develop creative approaches to infer customer preferences, intent, and tolerance from indirect behavioral signals. - Personalization at scale. A one-size-fits-all ad experience leaves value on the table for both customers and the business. We build systems that adapt ad load, placement, and content to individual viewers across 100M+ customers and 100k+ titles. - Small effects, large variance. Ad interventions typically produce 0.1-2% shifts in engagement, effects easily overwhelmed by natural behavioral variance. Measuring, attributing, and optimizing these small signals requires rigorous experimental design and causal methodologies. - Competing objectives. Revenue, customer engagement, long-term retention, and advertiser value are in tension. We develop principled frameworks to navigate these tradeoffs and optimize for sustainable outcomes rather than any single metric. A day in the life - Contribute to the research and development of ML models that personalize advertising decisions for 100M+ customers across 100k+ titles, with production deployment in mind - Develop deep learning architectures (multi-task learning, embedding-based representations) for customer behavior prediction at scale - Design and analyze large-scale A/B experiments, applying causal inference techniques to measure and optimize the impact of ad strategies on customer engagement and monetization - Partner with engineering to ensure models meet production latency and scalability requirements - Collaborate with product managers to frame business problems as tractable ML problems and translate findings into product decisions - Shape the team’s scientific roadmap, identifying high-impact research directions About the team Prime Video Ads is pioneering the use of Generative AI, Deep Learning and Causal ML to empower the next generation of Ads experience in Prime Video. Our vision is to build the world’s most valuable and differentiated ad-supported streaming platform: one where every ad is relevant to the viewer, and every dollar spent by an advertiser delivers measurable results. We are seeking lead applied scientists who have demonstrated experience in advancing state of the art ML algorithms, particularly in Personalization, Relevance, Casual Inference and Gen-AI areas. Your role will be to deliver these innovations as production-ready systems at Amazon scale.

We are venture backed and work with U.S.-based health systems and data providers. What you'll do As a Data Engineer II at Knit Health, you'll be a foundational member of a small, high-impact team building the data infrastructure behind our clinical AI platform. You'll help develop the clinical world data model that powers our AI systems, transforming complex healthcare data into reliable inputs for model training, research, and real-world applications. Design, build, and maintain data pipelines and infrastructure at scale, collaborating closely with our science, AI, and product teams. Expand our data integrations to new clinical and healthcare data sources, including the processing, modeling, and quality safeguards needed for reliable downstream use. Build and optimize large-scale, data processing systems for performance, scalability, and reliability. Drive data and product integrations with healthcare clients deploying our AI models. Help shape our data architecture and establish standards for data quality, testing, documentation, and observability. Minimum qualifications We're looking for candidates with strong engineering fundamentals, experience building production data systems, and the ability to independently solve complex technical problems. Systems thinking and problem-solving: Ability to reason from first principles, understand how complex systems work, and independently design and troubleshoot solutions without relying exclusively on off-the-shelf tools. Data engineering fundamentals: Strong understanding of data modeling, ETL/ELT, orchestration, database architecture, and data quality, including the underlying principles that make data systems scalable and reliable. Large scale data processing: Hands-on experience processing large datasets using Spark or comparable frameworks, with an understanding of distributed computing, performance, and scalability. Engineering experience: Approximately 4-6 years of professional data engineering experience, or equivalent hands-on experience designing, building, and maintaining production data pipelines and infrastructure. Programming proficiency: Strong Python and SQL skills, including complex queries, data transformations, and writing clean, maintainable, well-tested code. Cloud infrastructure: Hands-on experience with a major cloud platform such as Azure, AWS, or GCP. We value demonstrated engineering capability over a specific educational path. A background in computer science, engineering, mathematics, physics, or a related technical discipline is valuable, but we also welcome candidates who have developed equivalent expertise through hands-on experience. jobs.jd_excerpt: Who we are About Stripe Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career. About The Team The Radar ML team builds the machine learning systems that power Stripe’s Radar fraud and abuse product suite. Our models make real-time decisions across a significant share of internet commerce - helping businesses stop fraud, increase authorization, and grow safely. By turning economy-scale datasets into compelling ML products, the team directly improves customer outcomes and drives meaningful revenue for Stripe. The team is growing, and expanding into multiple new areas. We are building abuse protections across the full customer life-cycle, adaptive and customizable fraud systems for enterprises, and risk intelligence for 50+ global payment methods. What you’ll do You will own ML problems from conception to production: analyzing new fraud and abuse patterns, exploring large-scale datasets, experimenting with model architectures, designing evaluations, deploying models, and monitoring performance. Your work may include developing transformer architectures for payment data, building graph-powered intelligence across consumers, leveraging LLMs to detect emerging attacks, or rapidly prototyping new protections with frontier AI labs. You will have opportunities to ship 0→1 products, and to improve mission-critical ML models operating at Stripe scale. Responsibilities Build, train, evaluate, and deploy models that detect fraud and abuse across Stripe’s global network. Investigate emerging fraud and abuse patterns, identify where ML can help, and rapidly develop effective solutions. Design features, datasets, evaluation methods, and experiments for noisy, delayed, and adversarial environments. Improve model architectures, training methods, and production systems to increase model quality, coverage, and adaptability. Monitor production behavior and improve models as data, customer needs, and attack patterns change. Balance model quality with legitimate-user impact, latency, reliability, and operational complexity. Partner with engineering, product, data science, risk experts, and leading Stripe users to turn modeling improvements into differentiated Radar products. Contribute to reusable tools and AI-assisted workflows that help the team develop and operate ML systems more effectively. Who you are You are a fast, pragmatic problem solver with deep ML expertise and a bias toward action. You are excited to work at the frontier of payments and AI - turning advances in machine learning into production systems that address new forms of fraud and abuse. You’ve built ML models and shepherded them to production, landing impact for users. We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. Minimum Requirements 2+ years of experience developing, evaluating, and deploying machine learning models in a production environment. Strong foundations in machine learning, data analysis, statistics, model evaluation, and experiment design. Strong programming and software-engineering skills, with experience writing tested, maintainable code for production ML applications. Experience building or operating production ML systems, including one or more of large-scale data and feature pipelines, distributed model training, low-latency inference, model deployment, or production monitoring. Ability to investigate ambiguous problems, reason from data, and choose pragmatic technical approaches. Ability to communicate technical ideas and results clearly and collaborate effectively across disciplines. You might start by looking into an alarm from an overnight data job that feeds a finance control. Then you meet an accounting partner to design how a manual review could run automatically. After lunch, you write code and tests and ship the change through an automated pipeline the same day. Some weeks, you test a new AI model against an evaluation set to see if it gives better answers. jobs.jd_excerpt: <div class="content-intro"><p>Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.</p></div><h2>About The Team</h2> <p>The Sentry Tower Software team develops robotic systems that provide force protection capabilities, monitoring the perimeter of secure areas, land or sea, for approaching people, vehicles, and vessels. We live in a world where security officers are increasingly overwhelmed by sensor data feeds. Our products leverage advanced sensor fusion and autonomy to seamlessly render activity in the environment to Lattice’s common operating picture.</p> <h2>About the Job</h2> <p>Every Sentry Tower we ship, across Counter-Intrusion and Air Defense, boots from a common software platform: a NixOS-based overlay that defines the base images, the system services, the compute configuration for each hardware generation, and the network topology that ties the tower’s payloads together. That platform is the foundation the entire product line stands on, and we are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to own it.</p> <p>This is a systems and infrastructure role with unusually direct product consequences. The tower’s network is not a datacenter network: it is a set of VLANs and bridges carrying camera, radar, GPS, and sensor-board traffic over a mix of mesh radio, cellular, and satellite backhaul, on hardware that sits at the far end of a very long support loop. When a business line adds a new payload with its own switch, or when a routing priority is wrong, the failure shows up in the field. You will own the topology as a contract: define it, document it, review changes against it, and make the correct integration the easy one.</p> <p>You will also be a primary steward of our build and configuration system. Our images are fully declarative and reproducible, spanning several compute generations and a dozen product variants, and we are actively consolidating legacy per-product configurations into a common, composable base.</p> <p>Our Product:&nbsp;<a href="https://www.anduril.com/sentry">https://www.anduril.com/sentry</a></p> <h2>WHAT YOU’LL DO</h2> <ul> <li>Own the shared base of our NixOS overlay: system modules, compute platform definitions, common tower services, and the image definitions that every product variant composes from.</li> <li>Own the tower network topology end to end: VLAN and subnet allocation, bridging, link ranking and failover across heterogeneous backhaul, NAT and firewall policy, and the physical-port-to-payload mapping for each carrier board.</li> <li>Define and AWS Applied AI Solutions (AAIS) is building toward a future where every business innovates with Amazon AI teammates. To get there, we build AI solutions that improve human capabilities and transform entire business functions. We create end-to-end products that surprise and delight out-of-the-box, making complex things easy and hard things possible, with no cloud experience required. We start with customers who embrace the future and build bridges to meet the rest where they are. We pursue ambitious opportunities with conviction, and we are looking for builders who share that mindset. AWS IoT Core enables billions of devices to connect securely to the cloud — and the Identity and Registry team is at the heart of it. We own the foundational primitives that give every IoT device its identity, manage its metadata, and govern how it interacts with the cloud at massive scale. As a Software Development Engineer on this team, you will design and build the systems that customers rely on to provision, authenticate, and manage their IoT fleets — from a single prototype to billions of devices in production. You'll work on challenges spanning distributed systems, security, identity management, and scalable metadata storage and retrieval, directly shaping the experience for some of the world's largest IoT deployments. This is a high-impact role where your work will be felt across the entire AWS IoT platform and by customers spanning multiple industries — from smart home and automotive to broadcasting and industrial automation. If you're excited about building foundational infrastructure that operates at Internet of Things scale and solving hard problems in device identity and registry, we'd love to hear from you. Key job responsibilities - Design, develop, and maintain core services that power device identity and state management for AWS IoT Core, serving billions of devices worldwide - Build and operate highly available, low-latency distributed systems that handle device provisioning, authentication, metadata and state management - Own the full software development lifecycle — from requirements gathering and design through implementation, testing, deployment, and production operations - Write high-quality, well-tested code and participate in code reviews to maintain a high engineering bar across the team - Contribute to system architecture by authoring and reviewing design documents, identifying trade-offs, and proposing solutions to complex technical problems - Improve operational excellence by building monitoring, alarming, and automation tooling; participate in on-call rotations and drive root cause analysis for operational events - Collaborate cross-functionally with other AWS IoT teams to deliver integrated customer experiences - Mentor and support fellow engineers through knowledge sharing, design discussions, and constructive code reviews - Identify opportunities to improve engineering processes, developer productivity, and system efficiency, including leveraging AI to automate workflows, enhance testing, and accelerate delivery A day in the life You'll spend focused time writing code — building new APIs, tuning system performance to reduce latency at billion-device scale, or improving provisioning workflows. You'll collaborate with teammates through design reviews and code reviews, and partner with other IoT Core teams on cross-cutting features. Some days you'll dig into customer escalations, tracing issues through logs and metrics. Other days you'll experiment with AI tools to improve engineering processes. No two days are the same, but every day you're building the foundation that enables billions of devices to connect to AWS IoT. The Identity and Registry team owns the foundational services at the core of AWS IoT — device identity, registry, shadow, and provisioning. We build and operate systems that enable billions of devices to securely connect, be managed, and interact with the cloud. Our team values operational excellence, customer obsession, and a strong ownership culture where every engineer has a direct impact. We're a collaborative group that enjoys tackling hard distributed systems problems together, and we're committed to growing each other through mentorship and open technical debate. We're looking for builders who are excited to work at IoT scale. About the team ABOUT AWS: Diverse Experiences Amazon values diverse experiences. AstraZeneca is looking for a Scientist to join the NGS & Bioinformatics group within Cell Therapy Translational and Safety Sciences (CT-TSS). In this data engineering-focused role, you will build and maintain the data architecture, workflows, and computing environments that turn single-cell RNAseq and other NGS data into reliable, well-annotated, AI-ready datasets across our cell therapy pipeline (CAR/TCR/in vivo). Your expertise will be crucial in enabling translational and safety science insights and advancing our programs for patients. Accountabilities Design, build, and maintain scalable data architecture and data workflows that support single-cell RNAseq and other NGS data generated across Cell Therapy clinical and translational programs. Develop, automate, and optimize reproducible data processing pipelines (e.g., Cell Ranger, Nextflow/Snakemake-based workflows) from raw sequencing output through to analysis-ready datasets. Manage and administer NGS data across Linux servers, high-performance computing clusters, and cloud computing environments, ensuring efficient storage, compute scaling, and data lifecycle management. Establish data standards, metadata frameworks, and data quality checks aligned with FAIR principles to ensure NGS datasets are traceable, harmonized, and reusable across programs. Lead metadata annotation efforts for NGS and single-cell datasets, including sample, clinical, assay, and processing metadata, using controlled vocabularies and ontologies to ensure consistent, accurate, and searchable annotation. Ensure data is AI-ready by curating, harmonizing, and structuring NGS and single-cell RNAseq datasets (with complete metadata, versioned lineage, and quality controls) so they can be readily used for machine learning and AI model development. Partner with bioinformaticians, translational and safety scientists, and wet-lab teams to understand analytical needs and translate them into robust data engineering solutions. Implement version control, containerization, and documentation best practices, and contribute to a shared code repository and team standards for bioinformatic and data engineering work. Coordinate with IT, data engineering, and external vendors/CROs on data transfer, ingestion, integrity (e.g., checksum/manifest verification), and access controls for sequencing data. Monitor pipeline performance and troubleshoot failures, data quality issues, and infrastructure bottlenecks to maintain reliable, timely data delivery. Support integration of single-cell RNAseq data with clinical, biomarker, and other multi-omic datasets to enable translational and safety science insights. Document methodologies, workflows, and data lineage, and communicate technical concepts clearly through reports, presentations, and cross-functional discussions. Stay current with advances in data engineering, cloud technologies, and single-cell/NGS data tools, and apply them to continuously improve team capabilities. Every system runs through what we build. The service you own is on the path for all of them, and the people who run this hardware depend on it every day. What's the challenge? You need to have the ability to work within a fast moving and startup-like environment in a large company. You will identify solutions, trying ideas, given space to fail and iterate to produce products that your customers love. What you will do? You own a service in the management plane, in provisioning, monitoring, telemetry, software delivery, or diagnostics, depending on where the team needs you. You read logs and reason across process and system boundaries, you ship in small verifiable steps, and you turn requirements into a service other people rely on. You build the offline software-update service and prove the signed bundle applies and recovers cleanly. You design each system against the interfaces the platform exposes and turn architecture decisions into APIs and tools a customer runs without you in the loop. About the team Our team builds the software suite for provisioning, monitoring, software delivery, and the diagnostics of Trainium systems, and we build all of it on open, standard interfaces.
